# Install and build Edva

Edva currently targets Linux hosts. Install `libLLVM-18` system-wide and make
sure `clang` and Nushell (`nu`) are on `PATH`. LLVM 18 is a link-time
requirement of the compiler; another installed LLVM version does not replace it.

## File extension

Edva source files use the official file suffix **`.dva`** (for example, `main.dva`).

## Building the compiler

To build or incrementally recompile `edva` without running tests:

```sh
make edva
```

If `./edva` is not present, `make` automatically bootstraps the compiler from
`seed/ir/` using `clang`.

To regenerate operator and token tables, build `edva`, and run the entire test suite:

```sh
./build.sh
```

To verify a successful build:

```sh
./edva --help
```

If linking cannot find LLVM, confirm that the LLVM 18 development package is
installed. The build script consults `llvm-config` when it is available. If
the compiler can emit IR but cannot produce a binary, check that `clang` is on
`PATH`.

## Fixed-point verification

To verify compiler stability and self-hosting integrity through a 2-stage bootstrap:

```sh
make fixed-point
```

This procedure:
1. Compiles all modules to Stage 1 LLVM IR with the existing `./edva` and links `edva_stage1`.
2. Uses `edva_stage1` to compile all modules again to Stage 2 LLVM IR.
3. Asserts that all Stage 1 and Stage 2 IR outputs are byte-identical.
4. Promotes the verified `edva_stage1` to `./edva`.

## Compiling programs

Compile and run a `.dva` program:

```sh
./edva program.dva -o program
./program
```

For a different target, pass a target triple and provide a compatible clang
and linker:

```sh
./edva program.dva -target aarch64-linux-gnu
```

See the [CLI reference](../reference/edva-cli.qmd) for the complete options.
